Operations

General analytical steps, defined by what they accomplish rather than how. Each operation can be carried out by one or more methods.

  • Read preprocessing

    Remove adapters, primers, and low-quality sequence so downstream steps work from clean reads.

    • Amplicon primer trimming
    • Quality and adapter trimming
  • Site masking

    Exclude genomic regions whose variation would mislead downstream comparison.

    • Custom masking
    • Mobile element masking
    • Repeat and paralog masking
  • Genome assembly and variant calling

    Reconstruct each sample's genome, or the differences between samples, from its sequencing reads.

    • De novo assembly
    • Reference-based SNP calling
    • Reference-based consensus calling
    • Reference-free SNP calling
  • Genome alignment

    Arrange per-sample genome sequences so that equivalent positions line up across every sample.

    • Multiple sequence alignment
  • Recombination filtering

    Identify and remove variation introduced by recombination so the remaining signal reflects vertical descent.

    • Clonal frame inference
    • Iterative recombination detection
  • Phylogenetic inference

    Reconstruct the evolutionary relationships among samples from an alignment.

    • Bayesian phylogeny
    • Maximum likelihood phylogeny
    • Time-scaled phylogeny
